A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same S3T research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated storage-cost and broader-impact material.

before.justification: v2 reports original fine-tuning, deletion, and simulation results across vision and language tasks, including Table 1, Figures 5–9, and Appendix C.3.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds experiments on non-uniform deletion priors, ProtoSISA weight sensitivity, and ensembling models trained on different slice sequences.

M1.justification: v3 adds an experimental inference variant that ensembles models trained on different sequences within a shard (Appendix C.3, Figure 16). v2 describes selecting one best-performing model per shard before ensembling across shards. The default training, sequence-selection, and deletion algorithms remain unchanged.

E1.justification: All benchmark datasets remain. v3 extends deletion-rate evaluation to requests sampled from non-uniform priors (Figure 15 center); v2 used such priors for sequence-selection evaluations while its deletion-rate experiments used uniform requests.

E2.justification: The comparator methods remain unchanged, including SISA, ProtoSISA, full training/retraining, sequential PEFT training, and the sequence-sampling alternatives. The new ProtoSISA analysis sweeps parameters of an existing baseline.

E3.justification: New Appendix C.3 protocols vary budget with m=5 and L=32 under non-uniform deletion, sweep ProtoSISA weights 0.9, 0.5, and 0.3, and test ensemble sizes 1–10 using ViT-base on CIFAR-100 with m=5 and L=4. Existing protocols and Table 2 hyperparameters are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix C.3 adds focused analyses of budget sensitivity under non-uniform deletion, ProtoSISA mixing-weight sensitivity, and accuracy versus sequence-ensemble size (Figures 15–16). Existing deletion, layer-allocation, sequence-selection, training-time, and storage analyses remain.

E5.justification: Table 1's parenthetical uncertainty entries and the ten-prior averaging used for sequence-selection comparisons are retained. New plots continue existing reporting practices; no new run counts, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures are specified.

E6.justification: v3 adds non-uniform deletion-rate results, small benefits from lower ProtoSISA weights after many deletions, and ensemble accuracy that initially increases and then plateaus around 90.6–90.7% (Figures 15–16). Existing benchmark and storage results remain unchanged. These are additional results under specified settings, not revisions establishing same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Definition 1, Lemmas 1–3, sequence-scoring equations, and Appendix A proofs retain the same mathematical content. Edits to proof prose are grammatical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning PEFT parameter isolation, budgeted diverse sequence training, improved deletion capabilities, and performance retention.

C2.justification: New Appendix D explicitly discusses expensive training for larger models and high budgets, and motivates sample-efficient PEFT for small modular components. v3 also interprets the new non-uniform-prior results as greater deletion capacity. The malicious-deletion caveat already appeared in v2.

D1.justification: v3 adds an implementation repository address and a reproducibility statement reporting supplementary code submission. It also specifies hours for Figure 9's deletion time and explains ProtoSISA's weighted logit combination. Existing hardware, optimizer, and training hyperparameters are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works are unchanged, as is S3T's positioning relative to SISA, approximate unlearning, and complementary partitioning or adapter approaches.

P1.justification: v3 makes limited grammatical edits, adds reproducibility and ethics statements and a limitations appendix, reorders the storage discussion, and updates publication and author-contact text. The main narrative and section organization remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds shard labels to Figure 1, expands Figure 15 from one plot to three, and introduces Figure 16. It moves Table 2's caption above the table, relocates Table 3, and adjusts spacing and pagination while retaining the other displays.

improvement.justification: The new ProtoSISA sensitivity and ensemble-size tests help assess previously untested choices, while explicit limitations and implementation access information improve practical usefulness. These are limited gains over a stable paper. The non-uniform-prior analysis is less conclusive: its comparison with Figure 6 uses different slice counts, 32 versus 64, and its highly variable curve weakly supports the stated gradual budget trend.
